title: Authorization Wave Migration: Schedule, Safety Nets, and SIEM Sampling Strategy
content:
Context and intent:
This document recommends a staged ‘wave’ migration plan for RBAC v2 that prioritizes low-risk services, builds confidence via canary traffic and synthetic forensics probes, and standardizes SIEM sampling and evidence exports to preserve audit fidelity. The intent is pragmatic: minimize user-facing authorization regressions while producing high-quality telemetry for downstream compliance and incident investigations.

High-level goals:
- Move teams to RBAC v2 with minimal outages and clear rollback paths.
- Ensure audit logs retain full evidentiary context (pre/post-change) for 90 days in primary SIEM, 1 year cold store.
- Automate evidence collection for each migration wave so compliance can verify snapshots of entitlement state.
- Implement a SIEM sampling policy that balances cost and forensic needs (dense sampling for risky operations, sparse for read-only).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to host-level and console-level entitlements, service-to-service tokens, and delegated claims.
- Does not cover identity provider (IdP) migration; we assume stable IdP mappings exist.
- Requires runtime flags in serving and console codepaths to run dual-evaluation and emit shadow-audit entries.

Key definitions (for this doc):
- Wave: a logical group of services and teams migrated together (by risk profile).
- Shadow-eval: evaluate RBAC v2 in parallel to RBAC v1 and emit non-enforced audit events.
- Evidence snapshot: point-in-time export of the permission graph + sampled access events.
- Forensic probe: synthetic request patterns used to trigger and validate audit path coverage.

Wave plan (recommended order and rationale):
Wave 0 — Platform infra (non-customer-facing internal infra) — 2 weeks
  - Purpose: exercise migration tooling without external BL impact.
  - Activities: enable shadow-evals, run synthetic probes, verify SIEM export.

Wave 1 — Low-risk services (batch jobs, telemetry exporters) — 3 weeks
  - Purpose: validate batching/throughput characteristics of permission checks.
  - Roll-forward criteria: <1% mismatch rate between v1 and v2 shadow-evals, no production incidents.
  - Rollback criteria: any high-severity mismatch impacting job success rates.

Wave 2 — Internal developer tools (console read-only routes, CI triggers) — 4 weeks
  - Purpose: test UI-level authorization flows, attribute resolution for dev accounts.
  - Canary: 5% of traffic enforced, 95% shadow.

Wave 3 — Customer-facing read routes (stats/dashboards) — 4–6 weeks
  - Purpose: ensure observable behavior and latency SLAs maintained.
  - Sampling: dense audit for write-ish operations, sparse for GETs.

Wave 4 — Write operations and admin flows — 4–8 weeks
  - Purpose: high-risk operations; require manual approval gates at each step.
  - Preflight: mandatory evidence snapshot and stake-holder sign-off.

Wave 5 — Cross-tenant and shared infra (RBAC boundary enforcement) — 6+ weeks
  - Purpose: validate cross-tenant guardrails and forensics for multi-tenant incidents.
  - Strategy: run extended shadow period, then small-enforced cohorts.

Safety nets and rollback playbook:
- Dual-eval and Graceful Fallback:
  - All services will support a dual evaluation mode where v2 decisions are computed in parallel. Decisions that differ are logged with full context (subject, resource, attributes, rationale).
  - Enforced mode will always include a ‘soft-fail’ option: if evaluation latency > threshold OR a mismatch rate exceeds configured limit, fallback to v1 decision.

- Circuit Breakers and Latency Limits:
  - Per-route latency budget for auth checks (default 25ms); if exceeded, increment counters and eventually fail-open for a short TTL.

- Evidence-preserving rollback:
  - On rollback we must: 1) emit a final snapshot of RBAC v2 policy state, 2) mark affected audit events as ‘rolled_back_candidate’ in SIEM via an enrichment tag, 3) freeze deletions for related policy artifacts for 7 days.

SIEM sampling and export strategy (novel approach):
Principles:
  - Sample density proportional to operation risk score. Risk score derived from: operation type (write/admin > read), principal trust level (service tokens < internal admins), resource sensitivity (customer data flagged > infra metrics).
  - Ensure determinism for forensic reconstruction: sampled events must include the same canonical identifiers across systems (request_id, trace_id, subject_hash, policy_version).

Sampling buckets (example):
  - High (always collect): admin create/delete policy, entitlement grants/revokes, cross-tenant access, failed auths for admin routes.
  - Medium (1:1–1:10 depending on volume): account-level writes, token issuance, role-binding changes.
  - Low (1:1000 or periodic aggregate): telemetry reads, metrics read-only APIs.

Export formats and enrichment:
  - Primary export: JSON-LD compacted event with fields: ts, request_id, trace_id, subject_id, subject_attrs, resource_id, resource_attrs, decision, policy_snapshot_id, reason_codes, matched_conditions. (Note: SIEM ingest will translate JSON-LD into our internal event schema.)
  - Attach evidence pointers (S3 paths) for policy snapshots and relevant graph subsets; do not inline large policy blobs into every event.
  - Tag sampled events with stable batch ids to enable grouping for investigations.

Forensic probes and coverage validation:
  - Weekly synthetic probe suite per wave: scripted sequences that exercise common and edge-case grant paths (e.g., delegated access chains, temporal-attestation flows).
  - Coverage metrics: percent of principal–resource pairs exercised by probes, percent of policy-edges observed in actual sampled events.
  - If coverage < threshold (default 85%), expand sampling temporarily for affected resource classes.

Evidence automation (implementation notes):
  - Snapshot cadence: on any policy change, emit a compact policy diff and assign a policy_snapshot_id. Weekly full graph exports for long-term forensic storage.
  - Automate pull-request gating: every PR that touches entitlement resolution must include a local simulation run against a labeled dataset and a regression report (mismatch counts, false positives/negatives). Attach reports as links in CI artifacts.
  - SIEM hooks: use a buffered export adaptor to avoid backpressure on serving runtime; adaptor batches events and retries with backoff.

Validation and rollout metrics (KPIs):
  - Shadow mismatch rate (v1 vs v2 decisions) per route — target <0.5% before enforcement.
  - Auth check latency P99 delta when v2 enabled — target <5ms increase.
  - Number of rollback incidents per wave — target 0 for Waves 0–2, <=1 for Waves 3–4.
  - SIEM retention accuracy: sampled events include policy_snapshot_id for >99% of high bucket events.

Operational checklist for each wave (short):
  - Pre-wave: run static policy lint, schedule stakeholders, create evidence-snapshot job, register SIEM sampling policy.
  - Canary phase: start with 1% enforced, enable synthetic probes, monitor mismatch and latency.
  - Ramp phase: increase enforced percentage only if KPIs green for 72 hours.
  - Enforcement: once full wave enforced, run expanded probe set for 1 week and lock deletion on affected artifacts.
  - Post-wave: run a compliance review and archive snapshot.

Open questions / decision points:
  - Policy versioning semantics: do we provide optimistic or strict version pins for long-running requests? Proposal: optimistic pins with policy_snapshot_id validation for multi-step transactions.
  - How long should policy artifacts be frozen post-rollback? Proposal: 7 days by default, extendable to 30 days for high-risk waves.
  - Cost model for SIEM sampling at scale — need finance input on acceptable ingestion budgets.

Next steps and immediate action items:
  - Owners: Evelyn (migration plan), Miguel (evidence automation), Priya (SIEM adaptor), Liam (canary infra).
  - Build: shadow-eval runtime flag and shadow-audit schema (2 sprints).
  - Integrate: SIEM adaptor prototype and sampling rules (1 sprint).
  - Pilot: run Wave 0 and produce a retrospective with sampled event QA and forensic playbook (target end date: 2025-04-25).

Appendix: quick commands and probes (examples):
  - curl -H "x-experiment:rbac-v2-shadow" https://console.redwood/api/resources/123?action=read  # triggers shadow-eval only
  - SIEM query (example): "policy_snapshot_id:ps-20250318 AND operation:grant AND severity:high"

Notes and informal observations (team scratchpad):
  - Early tests show most mismatches are attribute-resolution differences (org_id derivation). Need a standardized annotation library across services.
  - We should centralize a small library of canonical test principals and resources for probe reuse.
  - Communication: prepare a short runbook for support and on-call so they can triage RBAC mismatches during canaries.

End of document.
